title: Outlook: enhanced calendar-sharing architecture for delegates in new Outlook for Windows and Outlook on the web
summary: The briefing accurately reports the roadmap's overdue target and distinguishes the planned change from the documented shared-calendar model. The history-control command, licensing background and retention warnings are supported; no correction is required.

claims.claim: No admin UI for setting the upgraded shared-calendar synchronization history boundary is documented.

claims.where: controls[1].api; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-MailboxCalendarFolder -Identity <MailboxFolderIdParameter> -SharedCalendarSyncStartDate <DateTime> sets the shared-calendar history boundary.
claims.quote:
[-Identity] <MailboxFolderIdParameter>
[-SharedCalendarSyncStartDate <DateTime>]
The SharedCalendarSyncStartDate parameter specifies the limit for past events in the shared calendar that are visible to delegates.

claims.claim: SharedCalendarSyncStartDate is supported only for upgraded shared calendars.
claims.quote: This parameter is supported only for shared calendars that have been upgraded as described in Calendar sharing in Microsoft 365, and is not applicable to any other type of calendar or mailbox folder.

claims.claim: The history-setting command targets the shared-calendar folder in the receiver's mailbox, not the owner's original calendar.
claims.quote: Use the shared-calendar folder in the receiver's mailbox, not the owner's original calendar.

claims.claim: The history parameter requires FullDetails, Editor or Delegate access to the shared calendar.
claims.quote: Users need to have FullDetails, Editor, or Delegate access to the specified shared calendar.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: An upgraded shared-calendar copy includes events from up to one year before the upgrade date by default.
claims.quote: The synchronized copy includes events from up to one year before the upgrade date by default.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: In the improved model, Exchange Online synchronizes the principal's calendar to a local copy in the delegate's mailbox.
claims.quote: In the improved model, Exchange Online synchronizes the calendar from the principal's mailbox to a local copy in the delegate's mailbox.

claims.claim: The delegate's Outlook client synchronizes with that local copy.
claims.quote: The delegate's Outlook client synchronizes with that local copy.

claims.claim: The documented improved model requires both mailboxes to be hosted in Exchange Online.
claims.quote:
The improved experience requires:
The calendar owner's mailbox and recipient's mailbox to be hosted in Exchange Online.

claims.claim: The documented improved model requires explicit permission to the shared calendar.
claims.quote:
The improved experience requires:
Explicit permission to the shared calendar.

claims.claim: The documented improved model requires a supported Outlook client.
claims.quote: A supported Outlook client and connection mode.

claims.claim: Eligible existing shared calendars are upgraded to the improved model in the background.
claims.quote: Eligible existing shared calendars are upgraded to the improved model in the background.

claims.claim: That service-managed upgrade does not require users to re-share calendars.
claims.quote: The upgrade is service-managed and does not require users to re-share their calendars or accept new invitations.

claims.claim: That upgrade does not require users to accept new sharing invitations.
claims.quote: The upgrade is service-managed and does not require users to re-share their calendars or accept new invitations.

claims.claim: With shared calendar improvements enabled and a DPT archiving the delegate's whole mailbox, MRM archives shared-calendar folders after the retention period.
claims.quote: After the retention period, MRM archives any shared calendar folders that are in a delegate's mailbox

claims.claim: Revoking delegate access does not remove archived shared calendars from the delegate's Online Archive.
claims.quote: If you revoke delegate access to the shared calendars, MRM doesn't remove the archived shared calendars from the delegate's Online Archive mailbox.

claims.claim: Cross-tenant and internet calendar scenarios can have longer synchronization intervals.
claims.quote: Cross-tenant and internet calendar scenarios can have longer synchronization intervals. The interval depends on the sharing type and the recipient's calendar service.

claims.claim: Immediate synchronization in the documented improved model is a supported same-tenant scenario, not a universal cross-tenant expectation.
claims.quote: Same-tenant shared calendars can synchronize changes immediately when they use the improved model.

claims.claim: Calendar permissions granted by the owner determine the recipient's calendar access.
claims.quote: Calendar permissions determine whether a recipient can view or edit the calendar.
